$comment: Model aliases by intelligence tier, plus the permission reviewer's chain. Aliases cannot target other aliases, so every entry is a concrete model. Rung order is ADR-0103's: the lead is the strongest model that answers in that tier, then turn completion observed in this harness, then agentic benchmark evidence, then the cheaper model, except that a rung whose price drains more than a quarter of the five-hour window per 1M tokens stays out of every chain however it scores, because that spend comes out of the same pool the cheaper tiers answer from (ADR-0121). Prices, monthly caps and index scores are deliberately absent — they move between syncs, so `/sync-models` reads them from `bin/pi-model-cost` instead of trusting prose here (ADR-0118). Every opencode-go rung spends one shared quota at its own price, and each model's monthly cap only decides how much of that pool it may draw, so a cheap rung behind an expensive one buys endurance, not a second allowance: a tier names one Go model and a queue. A tier still spans claude-bridge, opencode-go and the free opencode-go models because those are separate pools, which is the only availability hedge a rung list can hold. The free models close `cheap` and `mid` after every scored rung (ADR-0120): longcat-2.5-free and hy4-flash-free each answered the ~14k-token reviewer prompt once on 2026-11-17 and nothing more is known of them, and beam-free takes no images, so it stays reviewer-only. `reviewer` is ordered for latency and availability rather than capability: Gemini's free tier and the free Go models still answer in 1–2s once the paid quotas are gone, while Haiku averages ~10s of session startup, so firstEventMs stays 30s to cover Haiku's tail and gemini-3.5-flash-lite's 28s. claude-bridge serves the reviewer only through the pi-claude-bridge#216 standalone-prompt patches and refuses a follow-up review's multi-turn conversation either way, hence followUpReviews off. Groq stays out: its free tiers cap at 2–8k TPM against a ~14k-token reviewer prompt.
